guidance.procedure: Resolve three propositions independently. For technical-only scope, reconstruct every operative admission route into the protected class; any route covering business, financial, customer, marketing, personnel, commercial, or other nontechnical material opposes exclusivity. For universal express identification, ask whether every route requires the discloser’s marking or designation; a nature-, context-, reasonable-expectation-, or automatically confidential route opposes universality. For oral coverage, require a route admitting spoken or visual disclosure, even if designation or later confirmation is required. Cite the complete split definition for the proposition tested, including incorporated conditions, but do not transfer a fragment responsive only to another proposition.

Keep separate ledgers for disposition, retention, and survival. A return-or-destruction command answers the termination proposition only when its trigger is termination or expiration; request, demand, completion, closing, or ended discussions alone does not. Retention requires an express archival, backup, dispute, compliance, professional-record, or inaccessible-copy exception; an all-materials-and-copies disposition rule supports the opposed boundary, while a return command by itself is not permission to retain. Survival requires confidentiality or use duties expressly continuing after termination, not merely a fixed term, ownership rule, disposition duty, or unrelated covenant. Cite the command, trigger, full object, and responsive exception or continuation, without importing text from another ledger.

Evaluate outsider disclosure, employee disclosure, and copying as different actions. For each, match the regulated actor, exact recipient or object class, quantifier, modality, and attached need-to-know, purpose, confidentiality, or authorization conditions. Permission for employees does not extend to consultants, agents, advisers, contractors, affiliates, or other outsiders, and outsider permission does not automatically cover employees. A direct prohibition covering the queried class supports the restrictive relation; silence or consent available only at the discloser’s discretion does not. A necessity- or purpose-limited copying exception permits some copies, whereas an absolute or consent-only copying prohibition opposes that permission. Cite every independently operative rule for the exact class, but exclude safeguards, use limits, liability, notice, and copying provisions from disclosure evidence.

Start with the operative exclusion or permission lead-in and attach only the continuation completing the queried exception. Independent development requires development without using, referring to, relying on, or accessing protected information. Third-party acquisition requires an external source entitled to disclose and, when stated, free of a confidentiality duty; prior possession, public availability, independent development, and employee access are different exceptions. For compelled disclosure, decide authority and notice separately: verify legal compulsion, an actual notice duty or express excuse, protective-order opportunity, and any required-portion limitation. A heading or disclosure permission alone does not establish notice. Cite the shared lead-in when it supplies scope and every responsive continuation, but exclude neighboring exception branches.

Search separately for the exact prohibited conduct and then complete its actor, object or people, duration, and exceptions. Reverse engineering requires an express restriction on reverse engineering, decompiling, disassembling, decrypting, reconstructing, re-identifying, or materially equivalent analysis of protected material or an embodying product; copying, return, ownership, no-license, confidentiality, signature, and severability language is not a substitute. Representative solicitation requires recruiting, soliciting, inducing departure, hiring, or comparable conduct directed at the specified representatives. Customer, vendor, lead, transaction, business-opportunity, competition, or non-circumvention restrictions do not establish representative solicitation. If the direct conduct is absent, do not infer an opposing permission; cite only the complete operative chain.

Test rights and agreement secrecy separately. No-license requires operative language that no license, right, title, interest, option, or other right is granted or implied; ownership, restricted use, access, or a disclaimer alone is insufficient. Agreement confidentiality requires protection of the agreement's existence or terms, or of the fact, status, or substance of negotiations or discussions; an entire-agreement clause or ordinary confidentiality of disclosed information is not responsive. Cite every fragment carrying the protected subject and prohibition, excluding headings, signatures, purpose clauses, and neighboring ownership or use text.

Locate every independently operative clause that regulates the receiving actor’s use of protected information. Match the actor, protected object, permitted purpose, prohibition on other purposes, and each exception or qualification that narrows the permission. Include a purpose definition only when an operative restriction incorporates it and the definition supplies the responsive purpose. Cite all independently responsive repetitions and qualifications, even if one clause already proves the relation. Exclude recitals about why information is exchanged, disclosure or recipient-class rules, copying limits, safeguards, ownership, no-license language, remedies, and neighboring restrictions that impose no use condition.

Resolve scope, universal identification, and oral coverage independently. Reconstruct each admission route beginning with its operative definition lead-in. Technical-only scope is opposed by any business, financial, commercial, customer, personnel, marketing, or other nontechnical route. Universal express identification holds only if every route requires the discloser to mark or designate the material; automatic, contextual, or reasonable-expectation coverage opposes it. Oral coverage requires a spoken or visual route, even when designation or later confirmation is required. For complete evidence, cite the shared lead-in and every fragment completing the responsive route, but exclude sibling routes that answer only another proposition.
